question: How does a Beets plugin named in configuration become an executable CLI command?

observations.text: get_plugin_names() reads plugin names from beets.config['plugins'] and excludes those in beets.config['disabled_plugins'].
_get_plugin() imports the plugin module beetsplug.<name> and returns an instance of the last concrete BeetsPlugin subclass.
load_plugins() calls get_plugin_names() and then _get_plugin() for each name, storing non-None results in the global _instances list.
commands() aggregates Subcommand objects from all loaded plugins by calling plugin.commands() on each instance.
_setup() calls load_plugins() then extends the default subcommand list with plugins.commands() to produce the full subcommand list.
The parser's add_subcommand() method appends each Subcommand to its internal list and sets the subcommand's root_parser reference to the parser.
In the main routine, after _setup() returns, parser.add_subcommand(*subcommands) registers all subcommands on the parser.
parse_subcommand() looks up the subcommand by name from the parser's subcommands list and parses its arguments.
The subcommand's func is invoked with the library and parsed options to execute the command.
A configuration with pluginpath and plugins: test results in the TestPlugin instance being loaded and its commands becoming available, as shown by the test assertions.
The CLI options --plugins and --disable-plugins can override the configured plugin list at runtime.
The TestPlugin's commands() method returns two Subcommand objects with names 'test' and 'plugin'.
